title: LEC-SEQ – Lecigon as Sequential Therapy in Advanced Parkinson's Disease: a prospective, non-interventional observational study of effectiveness, tolerability and patient satisfaction after switching to LECIG following failure of a previous device-aided therapy
summary:
In advanced Parkinson's disease, tablets often no longer work evenly. Pumps are then used that deliver the medicine steadily throughout the day. If such a pump does not help enough or causes side effects, a switch to a different pump system is possible. How well such a switch works has hardly been studied.
This study observes people whose doctors are switching them to the Lecigon pump anyway. The study itself does not change the treatment. Over one year, participants are asked questions and examined at four regular appointments in the Parkinson's clinic: how satisfied they are with their life and their treatment, how they are doing with movement, sleep and mood, and which side effects occur. They are also asked what they expect from the switch and whether these expectations have been met. There is no additional blood sampling, no examination with radiation and no additional medication.

interventions.name: Patients with advanced Parkinson's disease who are switched, for clinical reasons, from a previous device-aided therapy (apomorphine, foslevodopa/foscarbidopa or levodopa/carbidopa intestinal gel) to LECIG (levodopa/carbidopa/entacapone intestinal gel). The switch is made solely on medical grounds a

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Parkinson's disease according to the MDS Clinical Diagnostic Criteria (Postuma 2015)
2. Previous therapy with apomorphine, foslevodopa/foscarbidopa or levodopa/carbidopa intestinal gel for at least 3 months with insufficient efficacy and/or intolerable side effects
3. Clinical indication for continuous levodopa therapy via pump system (switch to LECIG) established by the treating physician
4. Written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
1. Severe cognitive impairment (Mini-Mental State Examination below 15 points)
2. Acute or untreated severe psychiatric disorder, in particular psychosis
3. Contraindications to levodopa, carbidopa or entacapone according to the summary of product characteristics
4. Severe medical comorbidity that would substantially impair participation or LECIG therapy
5. Insufficient command of German to complete the questionnaires independently
